Q1: Britain. A British flag (Union Jack) flies over the tower and fortress in frames 40–41, which are dated 14 Jan 1780. The town sits under that flag while it is surrounded.
Q2: The "Great Siege". Frame 23 shows the caption "1779 — The Great Siege" (21 Jun 1779). After that, camps of tents and a trench line are built on the land side, and ships gather on the sea side.
Q3: Not sure. The pictures never show food, starvation or empty stores. The siege camps on land and the ships at sea suggest the town is cut off, so hunger from a blockade is a guess. Nothing on screen states it.
Q4: Ships. In frames 47 and 53–56 a fleet of many sailing ships arrives and sails toward or around the town (Jan 1780 and Apr 1781). Frames 57–58 show cannon fire at night. The pictures don't make clear whether the fleet is a relief fleet that helps the town or an attacking fleet, so this is partly a guess.
